messages:
maria (infra): starting a canary cutover for model-serving v3.2.0 -> eu-west-1. initial weight 5% for 10m, then 25% if no errors. rolling out via gitops/helm. pls monitor GPU pool and net egress.

devops-bot: Autopilot: Canary rollout triggered by pipeline #4821. git ref: `refs/heads/release/3.2.0` -> commit `b4f9c12`. 5% traffic to canary target group.

chris (platform): seeing cluster GPU pressure in eu-west-1 already: nodepool `inference-gpu-6` avg GPU util 92% across pods. if canary grows we'll saturate.

maria (infra): ack. is there spare capacity in eu-central or a cheap burst pool? cost vs latency tradeoff?

chris (platform): eu-central has 2 spare nodes but higher p99 latency (20-30ms). Also additional capacity requires spot fallback config. If we failover, need to update the traffic-split in Helm values + update region selector in the gitops repo.

jen (sre): FYI the gitops operator reconciled and reverted our manual splitter adjustment earlier today (drift). we need to make the change in the repo, not via kubectl. That caused a 3m blip during the last test.

alex (eng-ml): if we move canary to eu-central, model KV cache miss rate goes up 2x in internal tests. Quality could regress for some users. prefer keeping traffic local unless forced.

maria (infra): plan: 1) pause automated scale-up (avoid adding spot nodes automatically), 2) bump canary to 8% manually (in gitops repo) and set fast rollback if error-rate > 1.5% for 2m, 3) prepare a blue/green handoff in case traffic split can't be increased safely.

chris (platform): on (2) — this is the snippet I pushed to branch `canary/shim` (for review):
```
canary:
  trafficWeight: 8
  rollback:
    errorRateThreshold: 0.015
    evaluationWindowSec: 120
regionOverrides:
  eu-central:
    prefer: false
```

maria (infra): note: terraform plan showed drift on `aws_subnet.redis_private` for the eu-west-1 pool. plan output: `-/+ change in place` with new `mapset` of secondary CIDRs. If we trigger AZ expansion, quota may block.

jen (sre): we hit that quota last month. Recommend setting rollout to prefer intra-region fallback first, not AZ expansion. Also add stricter health-check probes so rollback triggers quicker.

devops-bot: Alert: GitOps Operator detected out-of-sync manifest for `svc/model-route` (PR open: #1073). Reconcile attempt at 2026-06-12T09:12:30Z.

chris (platform): important: the git commit that updates the weights must also include the autoscaler annotation `redwood.io/burst-policy: block-az-expansion` or the operator will attempt to provision new subnets (and fail).

maria (infra): I'm about to open the PR to `infra/gitops` with both canary weight and the annotation. tagging @chris and @jen for review.

jen (sre): quick ask — add a canary-specific metric export for `kv_cache_miss_rate` and `inference_p95` so our rollback policy can consider quality regressions, not just 5xxs.

alex (eng-ml): +1. We had a silent quality regression last time when we only looked at 5xxs. I'll attach a small eval harness to the PR that runs inference on a canary prompt set and reports delta.

maria (infra): PR opened: `infra/gitops#214` — includes canary weight bump, `redwood.io/burst-policy: block-az-expansion`, probe tweaks, and a link to the evals in the PR description.

devops-bot: CI: helm render OK. GitOps: PR queued for merge; merging paused pending 1 approval.

chris (platform): approved. merging now. watch for reconcile.

devops-bot: Merge completed. GitOps operator applied split: 8% -> eu-west-1/canary.

maria (infra): canary in flight. monitoring panels up: p50/p95/p99, error-rate, kv_cache_miss_rate, cost burn. tagging oncall.

jen (sre): first 3 minutes look stable. error-rate 0.6%, p95 +8ms, kv_cache_miss +12%. keeping watch for 10m.

chris (platform): GPU pressure still trending up. if p95 crosses +25ms or GPU util >95% for 2min, we should auto-fallback to 0% and route to eu-central with the blue/green switch. make sure fallback action doesn't trigger canary rollback twice.

maria (infra): added fallback step in the rollout policy: `fallbackAction: setTraffic(0) then promote blue-green target`. Also added a lock so single rollback event only triggers once.

alex (eng-ml): eval harness reporting slight quality drift on 6% of prompts (low severity). keeping under watch but not triggering rollback.

jen (sre): 9m in — error-rate spikes to 1.7% for 40s -> triggers our rollback condition. However, operator didn't perform fallback because metric label was `deploy_target` vs expected `target`. mismatch prevented automation.

maria (infra): ugh. metric label mismatch. we rely on label `target` in the rollout policy. quick fix: operator config needs alias map. opening hotfix PR to `infra/rollout-config` to accept `deploy_target` alias.

chris (platform): manual step: I set traffic to 0% for the canary via the helm values and kicked the blue/green promotion. Confirming service traffic now routed to blue target in eu-central.

devops-bot: Rollback executed by user `chris (platform)`. Canary traffic set to 0%. Blue target promoted.

maria (infra): postmortem action items: 1) add label aliasing to rollout automation, 2) add canary eval metric (kv miss + inference delta), 3) codify burst-policy annotation in terraform module docs, 4) add preflight capacity check in pipeline to fail early if GPU pools < 10% headroom.

jen (sre): logging these items, will create tickets. we should also add an automated dry-run that simulates GitOps reconcile to catch drift between manual and repo changes.

alex (eng-ml): will run the eval harness nightly against canary branches to flag data-quality regressions earlier.

maria (infra): thanks team. will follow up with a short runbook update and the PR links. :white_check_mark:
